events.title: Containers block Islamabad approaches; PTI delays march
events.detail: Shipping containers and spiked metal sheets were placed on routes to the capital, including Attock Bridge. PTI leadership said it delayed the march because key approaches were blocked. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said supporters would not be allowed into the capital; CM Sohail Afridi said the aim was a peaceful rally demanding Imran Khan's release.

events.title: Three rounds of PTI-government talks collapse
events.detail: PTI held three rounds of talks with a federal government and PPP delegation, which collapsed on the morning of Oct 4. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi blamed KP CM Sohail Afridi; PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the main obstacle was the federal demand that the province take ownership of anti-terrorism actions launched unilaterally by the centre.

events.title: PTI long march sets off from Lakki Marwat
events.detail: Afridi led the march from Gandi Chowk, Lakki Marwat, toward Islamabad via Karak, Kohat, Peshawar and Charsadda, demanding Imran Khan's release. The convoy camped at Karak that night. Naqvi warned the government would not allow violence or anyone storming the federal capital.

events.title: Gandapur turns back at blocked Yarik toll plaza
events.detail: Former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, due to join the march at Gandi Chowk, turned back after containers blocked the Yarik toll plaza, saying he would not break the law.

events.title: Afridi leads march on outskirts of Peshawar
events.detail: Afridi led a PTI protest march on the outskirts of Peshawar on Oct 9. He had said he would announce the next course of action when the convoy reached Khairabad on Oct 8; reporting on what was announced there was not found.

events.title: Emergency and governor's rule imposed in KP
events.detail: After a cabinet meeting chaired by PM Shehbaz Sharif, President Asif Ali Zardari approved emergency and governor's rule in KP, suspending the PTI provincial government. The army was authorised to deploy in aid of civil power. Islamabad cited militancy and law and order; the arrangement could last about six months. Some outlets report the announcement as Oct 12.

events.title: Afridi and other PTI leaders taken into protective custody
events.detail: Police said Afridi and seven other PTI leaders, including KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and provincial president Junaid Akbar, were in protective custody. PTI aides had earlier described this as arrests; the picture was not fully confirmed.

events.title: PTI calls emergency unconstitutional
events.detail: PTI's chairman and parliamentary committee rejected the decision as an unconstitutional assault on provincial autonomy. Afridi aide Zulfikar Bukhari called it "a coup disguised as emergency".

events.title: Internet disrupted in Peshawar and Swabi; containers on roads
events.detail: Internet services were reported disrupted in Peshawar and Swabi, with shipping containers blocking roads and heavy police deployment. Neither the PTA nor the Interior Ministry had publicly explained the coverage of the shutdown.

events.title: Naqvi chairs Apex Committee in Peshawar
events.detail: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Peshawar to chair a high-level Apex Committee meeting on security at the Governor's House.

events.title: Report: talks had offered Imran Khan meetings and medical arrangements
events.detail: According to party sources cited by The News, the failed talks had discussed a possible meeting with Imran Khan, immediate release of his sisters, normalised meetings and hospitalisation if doctors advised. No final agreement was reached. Mahmood Khan Achakzai reportedly insisted on meeting Khan before calling off the march.
